<action type="say">
Great — we’ll plan for Friday 19 December 2025, 3:00–7:00 pm in Darwin.

Here’s a compact setup plan:

1) Pick a location (outdoor, with shade and facilities)
Options to consider:
- Esplanade / Bicentennial Park: central, grass, shade, sea breeze.
- East Point Reserve: big open areas, sea views, sunset, toilets, BBQs.
- Nightcliff Foreshore: coastal, playgrounds, BBQs, popular for community events.
When choosing, check: toilets nearby, BBQs or power if needed, parking, and whether a council permit is required for your expected size.

2) Permissions and basics
- Contact City of Darwin council to ask:
  - If you need a permit for a community picnic on 19 Dec, 3–7 pm.
  - Any restrictions on amplified sound, marquees, temporary signage.
- Arrange:
  - Public liability cover (if this is an organised community event).
  - Wet‑weather fallback (small indoor hall or “postpone to…” plan).

3) Equipment checklist
- Shade & seating: marquees/gazebos, picnic rugs, folding tables and chairs.
- Serving: eskies with ice, food tubs, serving tongs, paper plates, cups, napkins, rubbish and recycling bags.
- Comfort: insect repellent, sunscreen station, hand sanitiser, baby wipes.
- Power / lighting: extension leads (if allowed), battery lanterns for dusk.
- Signage: simple A‑frames or printed signs so people can find you.

4) Food and drinks (heat-aware)
- Safer in the heat:
  - Pre‑made sandwiches/wraps, cold salads (kept in esky), fruit (watermelon, oranges, grapes), crackers & dips.
  - Plenty of cold water (at least 1–1.5 L per person), plus cordial/juice.
- Avoid:
  - Creamy dishes sitting out, anything with mayo not kept chilled.
- Setup:
  - Keep all perishables in eskies, only bring out small portions at a time.
  - Provide jugs of water and cups on a central table.

5) Activities & simple schedule (3:00–7:00 pm)
- 3:00–3:30: Arrivals, set up rugs, light background music, kids’ bubbles/chalk.
- 3:30–4:30: Main picnic eating time, casual lawn games (frisbee, soccer, bocce).
- 4:30–5:30: Light organised activity (short welcome, community announcements, maybe a simple group game).
- 5:30–6:30: Relax, photos, sunset views, second round of food/snacks.
- 6:30–7:00: Begin pack‑up and rubbish collection.

To tailor this properly:
- Roughly how many people are you expecting?
- Is this mainly families with kids, adults, or a mix?
- Do you already have one of those locations in mind (Esplanade, East Point, Nightcliff, or somewhere else)?</action>

<action type="say">
Nightcliff Foreshore near a playground is a great choice for 40–50 people with adults and kids.

Here’s a focused plan tailored to that:

1) Exact spot & layout
- Aim for: a grass area within clear sight of a playground, with some natural shade if possible.
- Layout ideas:
  - 2–3 marquees/gazebos grouped together for shade over food and main seating.
  - Picnic rugs at the front (kids), folding chairs at the back/sides (adults).
  - One table for food, one for drinks, one smaller “welcome/info” table (with sign‑in, name tags if you use them, and a first‑aid kit).
- On the day, check:
  - Wind direction (secure gazebos with weights/sandbags).
  - Sun position (set things so guests aren’t staring straight into the late‑afternoon sun).

2) Permits & practicalities
- Contact City of Darwin to ask about:
  - A community event of ~40–50 people at Nightcliff Foreshore, Fri 19 Dec, 3–7 pm.
  - Rules for marquees, public BBQ use, and a small speaker for music/announcements.
- Confirm:
  - Nearest toilets and parking.
  - Whether there are any booking options or first‑come‑first‑served BBQ spots.
- Arrange:
  - One person as safety/first‑aid contact (with a stocked first‑aid kit).
  - A simple wet‑weather plan (e.g., postponement date or backup indoor hall).

3) Equipment for 40–50 people
Approximate quantities:
- Shade & seating:
  - 3–4 large picnic rugs.
  - 25–30 chairs (not everyone sits at once).
  - 2–3 pop‑up gazebos/marquees.
  - 3–4 trestle tables (food, drinks, welcome, activities).
- Serving & hygiene:
  - 100+ plates, 100+ cups, 100+ sets of cutlery, plenty of napkins.
  - 6–8 large rubbish bags (plus some for recycling).
  - Hand sanitiser at food and activity tables.
- Cooling:
  - 3–4 large eskies with ice/ice bricks.
  - A few extra water jugs so people can refill bottles easily.

4) Food & drinks (heat‑safe, simple)
For 40–50 people:
- Drinks:
  - Water: aim for ~50–60 L total (large dispensers + refill bottles).
  - Extra: 20–30 L of soft drink/juice if you want more variety.
- Food ideas that work in the heat:
  - Sandwich/wrap platters (about 1.5–2 sandwich “rounds” per adult, ~1 per child).
  - Big fruit platters (watermelon, pineapple, grapes, oranges).
  - Robust salads (pasta or grain salads with vinaigrette, not heavy mayo).
  - Dry snacks: chips, popcorn, crackers, pretzels.
- Food safety:
  - Keep perishable food in eskies, only bring out smaller portions at a time.
  - Label one esky “Drinks only” and one “Food only” to reduce opening/closing.

5) Activities for adults + kids
- Ongoing:
  - Lawn games: frisbee, soccer/footy, cricket set, bocce or quoits.
  - Kids’ corner on the rugs: colouring pages, pencils, bubbles, pavement chalk.
- Light structure (around your 3–7 pm window):
  - 3:30 pm: Short welcome + housekeeping (toilets, boundaries, rubbish).
  - 4:30 pm: Simple group activity (tug of war, relay race, or a short scavenger hunt for kids near the playground area).
  - 5:30–6:00 pm: Quick thank‑yous or community announcements, then relaxed time as the day cools.
- Safety:
  - Set a clear boundary line for kids (e.g., “don’t go beyond this path/bench”).
  - Remind parents/carers to keep an eye on kids near any water or roads.

6) Quick checklist
- Before the day:
  - Confirm council requirements/permit.
  - Arrange gazebos, tables, chairs, eskies, and basic sound (if needed).
  - Assign who is bringing food, games, first‑aid kit, and rubbish bags.
- On the day:
  - Aim to arrive by ~2:00–2:15 pm to claim a good spot and set up.
  - Set up shade first, then tables and seating, then food/drink stations and games.
  - At pack‑up, do a litter sweep to leave the area spotless.

To fine‑tune the plan: do you want this to be
- potluck style (everyone brings a plate), or
- centrally organised (you/your group provide most of the food or use a caterer)?

That will change how we handle quantities, budget, and coordination.</action>

Great, potluck with central basics works really well.

Here’s a simple way to organise it:

1) What you (hosts) provide centrally
For 40–50 people:
- Drinks:
  - Water: aim for 50–60 L total (e.g., 4–6 x 10 L dispensers + some spare bottles).
  - Extra: 15–20 L of juice/cordial (and maybe a small amount of soft drink).
  - 3–4 large eskies + plenty of ice.
- Fruit:
  - Enough for everyone to have a few pieces:  
    - ~3–4 large watermelons  
    - ~4–5 kg grapes  
    - ~4–5 kg mixed fruit (oranges, apples, pineapple, etc.)
- Staples:
  - Disposable or compostable plates, cups, cutlery, napkins.
  - Rubbish and recycling bags.
  - Basic condiments: salt, pepper, tomato/BBQ sauce.
  - Hand sanitiser at the food table.
- Infrastructure:
  - Gazebos, tables, some chairs, rugs.
  - A few lawn games and kids’ activities.

2) What guests bring (potluck structure)
To avoid everyone bringing the same thing, set broad categories and ask people to pick one:

Suggested categories:
- Savoury mains (quiches, pies, sausage rolls, pizza slices, roast chicken pieces, rice/pasta dishes).
- Salads (pasta salad, rice salad, coleslaw, green salad, etc.).
- Snacks (chips, dips, bread/rolls, crackers, cheese).
- Desserts (slices, cakes, biscuits, muffins — items that cope with heat).
- Extras (ice, extra drinks, picnic rugs, games).

Coordination:
- Use a simple shared list (Google Sheet, sign‑up form, or group chat) with columns:  
  Name | What I’m bringing | How many people it roughly serves | Any allergens
- Ask people to:
  - Label food with: dish name, vegetarian/vegan, contains nuts/egg/dairy/gluten.
  - Avoid items that spoil easily in heat (fresh cream, seafood salads, etc.).
  - Bring their dish ready to serve (and take containers home afterwards).

3) Simple invite text you can adapt
You can copy‑paste and tweak this:

“Outdoor Community Picnic – Nightcliff Foreshore

When: Friday 19 December 2025, 3:00–7:00 pm  
Where: Nightcliff Foreshore (near the playground – look for the gazebos and signs)

We’re having a community potluck picnic – everyone’s welcome!

We’ll provide:
- Cold water, juice/cordial and basic drinks
- Fresh fruit platters
- Plates, cups, cutlery, napkins and rubbish bags
- Shade, some chairs/rugs, and a few games for kids and adults

Please bring:
- A plate of food to share (savoury dish, salad, snacks or dessert)
- If you can, add your dish to the sign‑up list so we don’t all bring the same thing.
- Label your dish with its name and any allergens (nuts, dairy, egg, gluten, etc.).
- Optional: a picnic rug or chairs, and any favourite outdoor games.

This is an alcohol‑free/family‑friendly event (adjust as needed).  
If the weather is severe, we’ll post an update by [time/method] about postponement.”

- Assign a few roles:

  - 2–3 for food table setup and keeping things tidy.
  - 1 for kids’ activities.
  - 1 for welcome/announcements and lost‑and‑found/first aid.
- Have a “food drop‑off” table so arrivals know where to put things.
- Keep one section of the table for vegetarian/vegan/gluten‑free and label it clearly.

If you’d like, tell me:
- How you plan to invite people (email, Facebook group, flyers, WhatsApp, etc.),
